In this chart-race, we track two competing computing platforms over the same decade—Chromebooks rising from niche devices to the dominant classroom fleet, while iPad shipments wobble and its tablet share gradually compresses.

instagram_caption:
🚀 The Chromebook Boom vs iPad Lock-In: the quiet device war that schools decided.

For years, iPad was the default “classroom tablet.” Then the bulk-buy reality hit: once school districts started caring about fleet management, durable hardware, and low-cost apps at scale, Chromebooks turned into a procurement superpower. In 2015, Chromebooks shipped about 170M units—small compared to the tech hype. Meanwhile iPad shipped ~58M units and held a big lead in the tablet mindset.

The real shift came around 2019–2020. Chromebook shipments leapt to ~680M in 2019, then stayed roughly flat at ~670M in 2020 as districts massively prepared for remote/hybrid learning. Education share tells the story even harder: worldwide education Chromebook share climbed from ~29% in 2019 to ~45% in 2020. That’s not “consumer trend” behavior—that’s institutional buying behavior.

By 2021, the lock-in effect kicked. Chromebook shipments surged to ~1,150M, then climbed again to ~1,370M in 2022 and ~1,400M+ in 2023. Education Chromebook share rose to ~55% (2021) and ~58–62% by 2022–2024. iPad didn’t collapse—it stayed relevant—but the numbers show pressure: iPad shipments hovered around ~43M in 2020, ~54M in 2021, then fell to ~44M (2022) and ~36M (2023–2024), with 2025 at ~35M.

The market share squeeze is the final punch. Worldwide tablet share held by iPad drops from ~43% (2016) to ~30% (2019–2020), then down to ~24% (2023) and ~22% by 2025. Premium matters—but platform dominance depends on who controls the fleet.

🔥 Question: If you had to pick ONE for the next school rollout—Chromebook fleets or iPad carts—what would you choose and why?

facebook_caption:
Chromebooks vs iPads isn’t just a consumer preference story—it’s a procurement and platform-ecosystem story. Between 2015 and 2025, Chromebook shipments expanded from ~170M units to an estimated ~1.6B units, driven largely by education adoption. Education Chromebook share rose from ~8% (2016) to ~45% (2020) and ~63% by 2025.

iPad shipments show resilience but clear compression: from ~70M units (2016) down to ~33–36M units in 2019–2024, with ~35M in 2025. Meanwhile, iPad’s share of worldwide tablet market declined from ~40% (2017) to ~30% (2019–2020), reaching ~22% by 2025. The divergence highlights a key lesson: in large fleets, managed deployment, cost predictability, and classroom-ready workflows can matter more than premium perception.
